items.title: Tracking issue: Stabilize `uv.lock` format
items.reason: Closest historical analogue: it coordinated breaking uv.lock schema and content changes before version 1 was declared ready. It is completed version 1 work, not a duplicate.

items.title: Rename `distribution` to `packages` in lockfile
items.reason: A breaking schema change tracked by astral-sh/uv#4893. It explicitly invalidated existing lockfiles, providing migration precedent for a new major version.

items.title: Record workspace member default groups in lockfiles
items.reason: This recent change established version 1 revision 5 as the current baseline and illustrates that compatible additions use revisions rather than a major-version transition.

related.search_scope: Literal searches covered the exact title, “Lockfile v2,” uv.lock version 2, major-version bumps, and version/revision fields across open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. Conceptual searches covered format/schema stabilization, incompatible changes, backwards compatibility, migration, and upgrades. No prior version 2 tracker or implementation was found. astral-sh/uv#15220 was inspected but ruled out because it concerns rewriting to a newer backwards-compatible version 1 revision.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#22106 tracks planned format evolution from uv.lock major version 1 to 2. Source documentation defines major versions as incompatible and revisions as backwards-compatible. No incorrect current behavior is reported, and the completed version 1 tracker does not cover version 2.
summary: No existing Lockfile v2 tracker or implementation was found. The closest precedent is astral-sh/uv#4893 and its breaking-schema change astral-sh/uv#5861; astral-sh/uv#22010 establishes version 1 revision 5 as the current baseline.
draft_response: We’ll use astral-sh/uv#22106 as the canonical tracker for the breaking schema and migration work required for uv.lock version 2. The current implementation writes version 1, revision 5; revisions cover backwards-compatible additions, while a major version denotes incompatible format changes. astral-sh/uv#4893 is the completed tracker for stabilizing version 1, so it is useful precedent rather than a duplicate. As the scope is defined, please add the individual schema, compatibility and migration, and rollout tasks here.
